author: Hacktivism
body:
I was recently informed by a moderator that swearing is no longer allowed on the server. When was this rule put in place?

In my opinion, if a rule is in place, all staff should enforce it. It's really frustrating when I see a staff member warning someone for saying "fuck", while another staff member lets it go. I've seen this happen with my own eyes. This makes everything really unclear to the community. You can't have half the staff team enforce a rule. Everyone needs to be equal. Your infractions shouldn't be determined by which staff member was online at the moment, but rather how well you follow the rules.

TL;DR: Either have all staff members enforce this rule, or none at all.

Also, could a list of prohibited words be released? It would make things much clearer for us. We don't know what classifies as swearing, and what doesn't.

Added: I just re-read the rule, and it says:

Excessive swearing is strictly not allowed.

Does that mean that swearing actually is allowed, just not excessively? Or should the rule be edited to further clarify itself?

replies.author: TortouseMincer
replies.body:
Personally, I think swearing is great. Now don't be a skid who goes around saying "oh no mommy says people who swear have no vocab-oo-lairy". Swearing is a form of expressing yourself and it is offensive.

But, just because it's offensive doesn't mean other things aren't offensive. If I started using sexual terms and things that are not appropriate for younger children, personally I think it's worse. We've all heard the word fuck, shit, hell, ass etc. Someone's bound to have said it around you; and you tried using it not knowing the actual meaning and your parents shouted at you. You learnt your lesson not to use the words. We're not responsible for children parents are.

Therefore, I don't think common swear words should actually be banned. I think sexual terms and other more offensive things should be banned, but the main base swear words should be allowed if they are not being spammed.

Onto the point of it being offensive; I am a very dark guy. My humour is not-okay. You see swearing let's me see who people really are. I express myself in a wild manner and therefore I associate with those who also express themselves like that. It also show's friends from acquaintances. The other day I swore at pizza and he actually got offended. You see I thought for example that Pizza was genuinely a friend. Then he went along and started being very conservative which pissed me off. I found my real friends; other people would swear back at me. I associated with them. 

People like to express themselves in the manner they choose; as long as there isn't some 6 year-old looking up sexual terms or something dark I feel it's okay.

replies.author: vladthegreat100
replies.body:
Ok, now that I know what the post is about, here is my point of view.
You see a Mod verbally warning a player for saying "fuck". What choices do you have?
You can easily report the player to a Sr Mod + or to a Mod who will pass the message on
You can wait and try to figure out what happened before the verbal warn. Was the player excessively saying "fuck" or was it only once? If you find out or you think the Mod was abusing his powers contact a Sr + or a Mod who will pass it on.
And the least recommended which is this, complain on the forums about it creating more stress on the team, and what create a controversy that you could have fixed with the first two choices. It's that easy. Why need to make a simple post about it that will get the attention of the community that they probably have not seen since it hasn't come up until now and get them to get all mad for a reason they didn't know until recently. 
Yes we like hearing about a communities opinion but must we really make this whole controversy that could have been fixed by reporting the Moderator and getting a Sr + talk to the Mod to change his ways of moderating or to be more lenient/tough.
This is my opinion. You can happily counter my opinion and we can see where it goes :) But please don't get mad over it.

replies.author: KenjiKido
replies.body:
My view:

A "bad word" isn't a "bad word" when it is not used to offend, or hurt any feelings. Just like software. If it is good that means it is doing its function. If it has viruses, spyware, etc, it is malware because the prefix "mal" means bad. You have to separate them. I mean, if a kid says, "Shit!" out of sheer frustration of like homework, tell me what harm they are doing? That is just like saying, "Poo!". Poo is a natural thing that humans do. But, if it these words are directed at someone or used for sexual relationship, or spam, then you can start to punish a player. However, terms like "bitch" or used to offend someone. So. To conclude my point I will put this as a fair rule in my judgement.

"If a player is using a "bad word" as to offend, spam, or use it as a sexual term, then it is considerable of punishment."

I'm sure not many people will agree with me, and I only wish to share my view. I only wish to share my point of view. I am quite sorry for the negativism in this post, but I just wish for this server to be as one and be positive. Hence why I put smile faces after my posts. I know that Avicus is one awesome place! :)

replies.author: vladthegreat100
replies.body:
You think its bias? We are given a guideline, we follow it, not always directly through the guidelines. If we followed exactly what the ban guidelines say there would be plenty of people on the forums and in game who would have been temp banned first time and even a ban. But what do we do? We follow the guidelines to the limit of what we can, enforcing what we believe is fair. That is not bias. That is simply trying to be as lenient as possible.

I have heard this many times and I believe its time to come out.
"You guys are too lenient, be more strict!
You guys are too strict, be more lenient!"
This is what is happening now. Just a few months ago we were being told to be more lenient throughout the community, we became more lenient by following the guidelines accordingly but not to the extent where we would to what the ban guideline says word by word. This is just the Moderators response to being lenient and unbiased in their own way.
Now you want all of the Moderators to change or keep the guidelines but stick to what it says and not do what we think is right.
This came up just last week.
"Mods are acting cold and robot like"
That would be from following the instructions we are given from the majority/all/Sr + have given to us.
We follow an exact guideline and we will be called robots again. We continue with being lenient and chose the smallest possible punishment trying to give no infractions and we aren't lenient enough and we should change.
And this has been happening for the past months now.
For you guys thinking
"Oh the staff team ignores the community" Think again...
At the start of this week Peachy made a post about recent stuff that came up in a Sr Staff meeting and have made changes that you guys kept asking.
So please keep that in mind next time you call us out saying that The Staff Team doesn't listen to the community at all.

I'm not talking about moderators being too strict or too lenient; that's not what this post is about at all. Sure, you can follow guidelines, but every staff member should follow the same set of guidelines. THAT's what this post is about. I don't care about how strict or lenient you are. Some moderators know the rules. Some. That's not enough. Every staff member needs to follow the same set of rules. I'm fine with a moderator tempbanning someone for five hours for swearing, and another moderator doing six hours. That's not what this is about either. I'm not fine with one staff member saying that swearing is strictly not allowed, and another one saying it is. That creates extreme confusion, and this is what appears to be bias. 

Think about it. If you're in-game with a staff member and you say "fuck" out loud, you get kicked. Then you join a different game, say "fuck" again, and the staff member there thinks it's okay. That would just make me wonder how the rule got changed in the two seconds that I was kicked.

Also, regarding your other point about Peachy's post earlier this week. Your argument is completely invalid and irrelevant. I never said that you guys aren't giving us updates about the update. The staff are doing a great job at that. What I'm talking about is the fact that once you guys update a rule, the community should be informed. In this case, the rule wasn't changed; however, a staff member told me it was, which, once again, creates confusion. So please, read the thread again and make sure your argument is actually relevant to what I'm saying. Sorry if this sounds harsh, but it's true.

replies.body:
Well, if we do indeed get these rules put in place this should be the place to discuss it whilst on the topic. 
I think we can all agree there should be a rule put in place that gives set directions to staff upon the action that is taken when a person swears.

But what is really suitable within a Minecraft Server? 
Will this be discussed at the next staff meeting?
If so, is the staff's decision final or will the community have input?
